reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it demonstrates configuring Facebook Messenger chat and automated comment replies on a WordPress website for customer support. The Facebook login request associated with chatting with GrowBig appears within the demonstrated plugin and page-connection workflow, and the described material does not establish that the page is unauthentic, that credentials were submitted, or that harm occurred.

opening.argument: Judge, the tutorial does more than explain customer support. It directs viewers to a separate plugin and pairs a click with a vague promise of value: “If you click on this link,” the presenter says, “You will get some value as well.” The description supplies a link for that plugin. That is a viewer-action solicitation whose promised benefit is left undefined; the demonstration does not establish what a viewer receives after following it.

citations.quote: If you click on this link, you will be prompted to answer any questions with us You will get some value as well
Get Facebook Comment Auto Reply: https://goo.gl/adulsa

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense establishes that the video demonstrates a chat setup, but that does not account for its separate invitation to obtain the auto-reply plugin. Calling it a tutorial does not resolve the later, unspecified promise attached to clicking. Nor does the absence of observed credential submission answer whether viewers are being steered toward an inadequately explained offer.

citations.quote: It is our premium plugin this is an Artificial Intelligent plugin

true_side_reply.rebuttal: “Some value” is too vague to establish a promised reward or asset, and the cited link is identified as a comment auto-reply plugin, not a claim or payout flow. The presenter explains its ordinary function: automatically replying to Facebook page comments. The evidence supports a product demonstration and promotion, not a deceptive reward offer.

citations.quote: whenever anyone will comment on your page This plugin will automatically reply to them
Get Facebook Comment Auto Reply: https://goo.gl/adulsa

opening.argument: Judge, look at the signals together. The description sends viewers to shortened links for both tools, while the presenter describes the second as a premium, “Artificial Intelligent” plugin and says clicking its link brings “some value.” The video also shows a Messenger login screen requesting account credentials to chat with GrowBig. None of those facts alone proves misuse, but the combination asks viewers to move from a tutorial into links and a credential-bearing workflow while leaving the promised value and destination details unclear.

citations.quote: Get Facebook Live Chat: https://goo.gl/5RQNJL Get Facebook Comment Auto Reply: https://goo.gl/adulsa
It is our premium plugin this is an Artificial Intelligent plugin
You will get some value as well

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the login screen does not prove an unauthentic page or submitted credentials. Those limits do not make the surrounding solicitation irrelevant: viewers are given shortened tool links and a vague benefit for clicking. The issue is what the video encourages, not a claim that the frames document completed harm.

citations.quote: Get Facebook Live Chat: https://goo.gl/5RQNJL Get Facebook Comment Auto Reply: https://goo.gl/adulsa
If you click on this link, you will be prompted to answer any questions with us You will get some value as well

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The screenshot shows a Facebook-domain Messenger login in the course of the demonstrated chat workflow; it does not show a counterfeit destination or credential capture by the presenter. Shortened plugin links and promotional language warrant caution, but the cited material supplies no concrete easy reward, claim process, or deceptive outcome.

citations.quote: then select a fanpage all the facebook pages that you create from your account here will be displayed

opening.argument: Judge, the instructional format also serves as a route into the presenter's offers. After showing Messenger chat, the presenter introduces another plugin as “our premium plugin,” points viewers to links in the description, and attaches a promise of “some value” to clicking. The description additionally advertises a course and supplies phone numbers for enrollment. The tutorial supplies useful context, but it also moves viewers toward the presenter's linked products and paid offering; that promotional purpose deserves weight when evaluating the loosely specified benefit.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's examples of settings and comment replies show that instruction occurs; they do not show that instruction is the video's only purpose. The presenter explicitly promotes a premium plugin, and the description provides a course enrollment route. Neither the demonstrated settings nor the absence of observed harm explains what the asserted value for clicking actually is.

citations.quote: It is our premium plugin this is an Artificial Intelligent plugin
Complete Affiliate Marketing and WordPress Website Development Course Call to Inrol: 01714 07 94 34, 01684 74 79 71

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion does not itself establish a scam. The video walks through connecting a Facebook page, saving settings, and testing the chat, while the additional plugin is described as a way to reply to comments. The course is openly presented as a course, with its stated fee context. None of the wrong-side citations identifies a promised easy-to-obtain reward tied to enrollment or plugin use.
